files.document_title: Public Volume I, Figure 1.B.1 General Project Location Map, ETC Tiger Pipeline Franklin Farms Project, TRC, May 2026, accession 20260701-5406, docket CP26-549-000
files.fetch_route: FERC eLibrary download service (curl POST), then pdftoppm at 150 dpi
files.what_it_shows: A 1:336,000 topographic map of Richland Parish with the project boundary in yellow. The lateral starts south of Interstate 20 near Rayville and runs north across the interstate and US 80, then jogs east and ends north of Rayville near Cypress Creek and Louisiana Highway 183. Parish outline is dashed.

files.document_title: Public Volume I, Appendix A Figure 2 Project Location Map (Aerial), 1:120,000, TRC, May 2026, same filing, page 650 of the PDF, rendered at 100 dpi
files.what_it_shows: A larger scale aerial view of the same project boundary in yellow, showing the lateral running north from south of Interstate 20 across Highway 80 and to a jog east of Bee Bayou, ending west of Louisiana Highway 183.

searched: FERC eLibrary full text search for the phrase Richland Parish, which found docket CP26-549-000, the ETC Tiger Pipeline Franklin Farms Project.
The docket listing for CP26-549-000, including the public Volume I of the abbreviated application filed July 1, 2026.
The text of Volume I, searched for figure titles and the pipeline length.
Web search for the Tiger lateral and the Meta data center.
notes: The sheet row is the Franklin Farms Lateral. The FERC application says it is a 36-inch pipeline of about 13.24 miles with 1,000,000 dekatherms per day of capacity, starting at milepost 163.87 of the Tiger mainline south of Interstate 20 and running north under the interstate. The sheet says 12 miles, so the length is a little low. The alignment sheets in Appendix A-7 and the detailed route volume are filed as Critical Energy Infrastructure Information and are not public, but Volume I has a public statewide-scale location map (Figure 1.B.1) and a 1:120,000 aerial location map (Appendix A, Figure 2) that give a tighter fit. The FERC eLibrary page is a JavaScript application, so the URL checker calls it a JavaScript shell. The file was downloaded directly and read.
